note: Words and picks for the home page (tools/render_home.py). clips: the hero mosaic, cut by tools/hero_clips.sh from recordings on project pages (file is the clip name under site/media/hero/clips/). what: the six tiles, each a card drawing from tools/card_anim.py in front and a page picture behind (site/media/home/*.jpg are screenshots of the site's own pages). rail: smallest to Linux, with the motor-control F2800137 beside the AM13 (maintainer, 2026-10-30); id is the row in data/boards.csv, size the drawn board's class, photo the stage picture when no data/boardviz/<id>.json exists, hi one line on what it is or ran here, line the last serial line each board printed in portability/three-ways (site/one-app-eleven-boards.html). demos: six projects with a recipe (the renderer fails if one has none); clip names a hero clip to play on hover. build: the scene the home page scrolls through. drive: the browser tools.

demos.title: Doom on a Cortex-M33
demos.line: The engine runs on the kit and draws on the BoosterPack's 128 by 128 screen.
demos.alt: An LP-MSPM33C321A under the Educational BoosterPack, its small screen showing the Doom title

demos.title: 2048 on a 3.5 inch touch screen
demos.line: Swipe to play 2048 on a 3.5 inch touch screen; Game Boy and more share the project.
demos.alt: A finger swiping tiles in 2048 on a 3.5 inch touch screen wired to a development kit

demos.title: Handwriting recognized on the chip
demos.line: Draw a digit with your finger and the chip names it on the screen.
demos.alt: A finger draws a 9 on a small touch screen wired to a LaunchPad; the screen shows its answer

demos.title: Radar presence sensing
demos.line: Detected a seated person in every frame at 2 m and 4 m, one pass each, on the two radar settings that ran.
demos.alt: The IWRL6432BOOST radar kit with its LEDs lit

demos.title: A vision model on a Linux board
demos.line: TI's 14 ready-made vision models run on the board's AI accelerator in {{row:tda4/dl_inference_ms/mobilenetv1-mlperf-224-tflitert-tidl-c7x|.0f}} to {{row:tda4/dl_inference_ms/yolox-s-pose-640-onnxrt-tidl-c7x|.0f}} ms each; the 8 that also ran on its two Arm cores took 13 to 135 times longer there.
demos.alt: The SK-TDA4VM board with its heatsink, held over the bench with its cables plugged in

demos.title: Blink, then change the pattern
demos.line: Plug in the board, build the blink, then ask for a new pattern in plain English.
demos.alt: An MSPM0 G3507 development kit on a wooden bench, USB cable in, a green LED lit

rail.name: MSPM0 C1104
rail.hi: The smallest chip here. Blink, a voltage reading and the serial line fit in 1 kB of RAM.
rail.photo_alt: A LaunchPad kit on the bench

rail.name: MSPM0 L1306
rail.hi: The board the start script supports: first blink from a fresh clone.
rail.photo_alt: An LP-MSPM0L1306 with its USB cable in

rail.name: MSPM0 G5187
rail.hi: An MSPM0 with a neural processing unit (NPU) for edge AI models; the Sub-1 GHz link and the sensors pack ran here.
rail.photo_alt: The Sensors BoosterPack on an LP-MSPM0G5187

rail.name: MSPM0 G3519
rail.hi: The biggest MSPM0 here: 2048 on a 3.5 inch touch screen ran here.
rail.photo_alt: 2048 on a touch screen wired to the LP-MSPM0G3519

rail.name: MSPM33 C321A
rail.hi: A Cortex-M33 at {{board:mspm33c321a/clock_mhz}} MHz; Doom ran here on the BoosterPack screen.
rail.photo_alt: Doom on the BoosterPack screen on an LP-MSPM33C321A

rail.name: F2800137
rail.hi: A real-time control MCU for motors and power, with TI's own C28x processor core instead of an Arm core.
rail.photo_alt: A LaunchPad kit on the bench

rail.name: AM13E230
rail.hi: A real-time control MCU with a neural processing unit; motor control and edge AI models ran here.

rail.name: CC2340R5
rail.hi: Bluetooth LE; the gamepad and the asset-tracking tag ran here.
rail.photo_alt: An LP-EM-CC2340R5 beside its probe, LED lit

rail.name: CC2755P10
rail.hi: Bluetooth LE and 802.15.4 with a +20 dBm radio.
rail.photo_alt: A radio kit on the bench

rail.name: CC35X1
rail.hi: Wi-Fi 6 and Bluetooth; the Matter light, the DNS ad blocker and the asset-tracking hub ran here.
rail.photo_alt: The LP-EM-CC35X1 wired beside an LP-MSPM0G3519

rail.name: AM62L
rail.hi: Two Arm Cortex-A53 cores running Linux; the same app.c built with GCC and reads its voltage input through a Linux device file.
rail.photo_alt: Doom on the AM62L evaluation module

what.line: Each build that ran on a kit has its parts, wiring, steps and the code; one not yet run says so on its page.
Arduino, ESPHome, Zephyr, MicroPython, STM32, ESP32 and Pico code on a TI board: a port is code written for another board, moved over.

what.line: Every board on the same tests, with the method behind each number.
Flash a board, read its pins and memory, flash a motor demo. Chrome and a USB cable, nothing to install.
